etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from Middle French capable, from Late Latin capābilis.

definitions.definition: Able and efficient; having the ability needed for a specific task; having the disposition to do something; permitting or being susceptible to something.
(obsolete) Of sufficient capacity or size for holding, containing, receiving or taking in; accessible to. Construed with of, for or an infinitive.

quote.citation: 1672, Lord Herbert, The Life and Reign of King Henry the Eighth, page 594:
quote.text: The place chosen was the cathedral church, capable of about 400 persons.

quote.citation: 1775, Samuel Johnson, A Journey to the Western Islands of Scotland (Works 10.479), page 304:
quote.text: He has begun a road capable of a wheel-carriage.
